newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers on dlr covering by big players.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers on dlr covering by big players.

text.p: The ringgit made a 100-point recovery on widespread covering of short dollar positions, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Rumours went around that some of the big-time players were buying back their dollar shorts. In anticipation of that buying, others also bought heavily," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said some stop-losses were also triggered at 2.4860 level, which brought dollar tumbling down against the ringgit.
"There should be some fresh (dollar) selling in European time too," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said the ringgit was widely expected to remain in a 2.4680 and 2.4880 a dollar range in the near-term.
"The ringgit is consolidating after the recent run up. But there is a lot of dollar selling at the present levels," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore.
She said there was also demand for the dollar from Kuala Lumpur, which could offset some of the Malaysian currency's potential gains.
The ringgit has gained over two percent this year.
At 0700 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4755/65 a dollar.
